title: Build from CLIVE (1 of 2): file engineering objectives and report their progress
requested_outcome: Owner-approved direction: CLIVE becomes the one interface for building itself. Objective 1 of 2: CLIVE can file an engineering objective into the remote engineering loop and report its progress in plain words, with the owner approving each submission through the existing write gate. No UI changes in this objective. The loop reads JSON requests from the GitHub branch clive/control/owner-inbox at requests/<request_id>.json (schema clive.remote_engineering_request.v1; fields schema_version, request_id, title, requested_outcome, base_ref, base_sha, allowed_paths, acceptance_criteria, checks as a list of name, argv and cwd, target_branch, max_repair_rounds) and publishes clive/control/status:status.json (generated_at, adapter.intake_error, and requests with request_id, outcome accepted or refused, stage, stage_reason, blocker, candidate_sha, review verdicts, acceptance and integration). Rules the loop enforces and CLIVE must pre-check: request_id matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}(-[a-z0-9]{1,16}){1,7}$ and target_branch equals clive/objective/<request_id>; base_sha is a 40-hex commit; allowed_paths are repository-relative and never overlap the loop's protected paths (import PROTECTED_PATHS from app/orchestrator/objectives.py rather than copying it); requested_outcome is at most 20000 characters; max_repair_rounds is 0 to 5. Build: (1) app/engineering_bridge/requests.py - build and validate a request from structured fields, refusing without echoing any rejected value. (2) app/engineering_bridge/github.py - a small client over the GitHub REST contents API for the repository crooksldn-pixel/clive (configurable): read status.json from clive/control/status; read the inbox branch head and whether requests/<id>.json exists; create requests/<id>.json as one new commit only when absent, never overwriting and never forcing, and on any conflict re-read and refuse. The token is read at call time from the existing secret store (app/secrets) under the name github_engineering_inbox_token. When it is missing every call returns a typed not-connected result and nothing is attempted. The token never appears in logs, errors, tool results or cards. (3) app/tools/engineering_tools.py, registered through the existing @tool registry and bound in app/runtime.py like the other tool modules: a read tool engineering_status that projects status.json into plain words per request (queued, building, in review, done, blocked with the reason, needs the owner) with the candidate SHA when done; and a write tool submit_engineering_request using WriteSpec: prepare builds and validates the request and presents the title, what may change, the checks and the base in plain words; observe re-reads the inbox head and confirms the file is absent; execute creates it; verify re-reads the file and compares bytes; interaction tap_commit, irreversible. Fit the existing WriteSpec contract as it is; if it cannot express this write, report that as a blocker instead of changing the gate. Regenerate docs/phase4/TOOL_MATRIX.md with the repository's generator. If an existing test enumerates the registered tools, add the two new tools to its expectation and change nothing else in it. (4) tests/test_engineering_bridge.py with GitHub faked (no network): validation refusals without echo, the not-connected path, create-if-absent and refusal when the file exists, the status wording, gate staging of the write tool, and the token absent from every output. Do not change the gate, the action engine or any protected path. Provisioning the token is a later owner step and the code must work without it. An earlier attempt at this objective failed the ruff check twice; run ruff yourself and fix every finding before you report. Run every check listed below in your workspace and fix anything it reports before you report. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: a request built by the bridge passes the loop's own intake rules, and invalid fields are refused without echo
with no token configured every bridge call returns not-connected and nothing is attempted
submission creates requests/<id>.json only when absent, never overwrites, and is staged through the existing write gate for owner approval
engineering_status reports each request's progress in plain words
the token appears in no log, error, tool result or card
no gate, action-engine or protected-path change; TOOL_MATRIX.md is the generator's output
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
